content: Dog spinning was a ritual historically practiced in a village located in southeastern Bulgaria. In this ritual, a dog was suspended above a body of water using a rope. The rope was twisted repeatedly in one direction, either clockwise or counterclockwise, creating tension. Once the rope was released, the dog would spin rapidly in the opposite direction due to the unwinding of the rope. This ritual, which has its origins in ancient pagan traditions, was believed to serve as a method to prevent rabies. The first known mention of this practice in English appeared in a press release issued by the UK Green Party on July 29, 2005. The press release included a statement from Dr. Caroline Lucas, a Member of the European Parliament (MEP) for the Green Party, vice-president of the RSPCA, and a member of the European Parliament's cross-party Animal Welfare Intergroup. Dr. Lucas condemned the practice, describing it as cruel and stating, Dog-spinning is a barbaric practice and must not be allowed to continue into the 21st century. The Swedish newspaper Aftonbladet also reported on this ritual in March 2005. Historically, the ritual was performed annually in March, exclusively in the village of Brodilovo. However, following complaints from Bulgarian animal welfare organizations, the mayor of Tsarevo officially banned the practice in 2006.
